question.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]≈3.314\,81,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{9}, & 0<x<3, \\ \frac{1}{9}(2x-5), & 3\le x<5, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{5}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{5}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{9}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{5}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{9}(2x-5)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{5}\frac{1}{9}(2{x}^{3}-5{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{27}|}_{0}^{3}+{\frac{1}{9}(\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{5{x}^{3}}{3})|}_{3}^{5} \\  & ≈13.074\,07\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & ≈13.074\,07-(3.314\,81)^{2} \\  & ≈2.09\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $2$ decimal places.
